deadline.value: There is no single deadline; aim to apply by January for an October start. International funding comes mainly from the President's PhD Scholarship (rounds close 2 Nov 2026, 11 Jan 2027 and 1 Mar 2027) and from the few overseas departmental scholarships, which follow the same dates. The department's internal nomination deadlines for the later rounds are 25 Jan and 15 Mar 2027.
deadline.quote: Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 2 November 2026 and are awarded a scholarship will be notified by 31 January 2027. | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 11 January 2027 | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 1 March 2027

also.quote: So make sure you plan to submit your application on time, ideally by January of the same year.
Deadlines: Refer to the dates for the President’s scholarship on this webpage
Department deadline (for academics to put a candidate forward) – 25 Jan 2027

supervisor.value: Even if you are self-funded, you must first get a Materials academic interested in supporting you. They may interview you, and you name them on your application (only one academic per department).
supervisor.quote: Regardless of your funding needs, you must identify and secure the interest of a department academic whose research aligns with your background.

also.quote: To get a PhD, it is vital that you get a member of the academic staff to support your application, even if you are self-funded!

funding.value: Departmental scholarships cover Home fees plus a UKRI London-rate stipend, and only a few overseas departmental scholarships are offered each year. CDTs cannot fund overseas students. The President's PhD Scholarship is open to all nationalities.
funding.quote: Full funding for home tuition fees (UK, Irish citizens and EU citizens with settled status qualify as home students) | A few overseas departmental scholarships (no DLAs) are available each year.

also.quote: CDT's, unfortunately, cannot fund overseas students and most of the CDTs do not accept self-funded students.

entry_route.value: You are normally expected to hold or be completing a master's degree as well as a bachelor's at UK 2:1 level.
entry_route.quote: For admission to a PhD research programme, the College would normally expect you to hold or achieve a Master's degree, in addition to a Bachelor's degree at UK Upper Second Class Honours Level.

notes: Apply to 'Materials Research PhD' on My Imperial. Your application is shared only with the academic you name, who has up to five weeks to decide; the whole process takes about 6-9 weeks. The ATAS CAH code is 10-03-02.
